title: Seven days with death
intro: One short talk and one practice a day for a week. The traditions agree on little, but they agree that remembering death changes how we live. Go gently; skip a day whenever you need to.
author: wiser

units.title: The one certainty
units.intro: Start with the plain fact: everyone who is born dies.

items.note: What would I stop putting off if I took this seriously?

units.title: Mindfulness of death
units.intro: The Buddha asked monks to recall death with every breath.

units.title: Who dies?
units.intro: Advaita turns the question around: find who it is that is afraid.

units.title: The moment of death and after
units.intro: Tibetan teachers map the dying process and the bardo in detail.

items.note: Preparing for the bardo, a short orientation on the Rebirth hub.

units.title: Grief and loss
units.intro: Death is also what happens to the people we love.

units.title: Practising dying
units.intro: Plato called philosophy a rehearsal for death.

units.title: What remains
units.intro: End where the traditions point: the deathless, the Self, the open sky of mind.

items.note: What did this week change, if anything?

title: Rebirth across traditions
intro: Does anything carry on after death? One talk from each tradition that answers, then the classic texts to read for free.
author: wiser

units.title: The owner of my actions
units.intro: Theravada: actions have consequences that outlive this body. Start with the five remembrances.

items.note: Which of the five lands hardest? That one is your teacher this week.

units.title: The between-state
units.intro: Tibetan: between death and rebirth lies the bardo. Prepare for it the way you would for a journey.

items.note: What would you pack for a journey you cannot refuse?

units.title: Who dies?
units.intro: Advaita: before asking what is reborn, find who it is that fears death.

items.note: Notice the difference between thinking about the seeker and looking for it.

units.title: Remembering, both ways
units.intro: Early suttas and the Platonists both kept death in daily view. Recollect the round; practise dying.

items.note: Two traditions, one exercise: what changes when death is remembered daily?

units.title: Urgency, not fear
units.intro: Close with the shared ground: mindfulness of death as urgency for practice, not fear.

items.note: What would you stop putting off if you took impermanence seriously?

title: Kashmir Shaivism: a first syllabus

title: Visualisations: the Tibetan deity practice primer
intro: Orientation only. Deity yoga is taught in Tibetan Buddhism after an empowerment and with a teacher; this primer explains what it is and why it is practised, through talks by teachers of the tradition. It does not teach the visualisations themselves.
author: wiser

title: Metta in four traditions

author: wiser

title: Middle Pillar week
intro: One outline, seven sittings. Each day adds one centre to the pillar, then rests in the circulation. Ten minutes a day. This is orientation only: the full form is learnt in the order or from a qualified teacher.
author: wiser

units.title: The pillar
units.intro: The pillar first: light along the midline, crown to feet. Nothing else.

items.note: Can you feel the midline as one continuous line? If not, that is the work.

units.title: Crown
units.intro: Add the crown: brilliant white above the head, the source of the light.

items.note: White first: the colour of undifferentiated light.

units.title: Throat
units.intro: Add the throat: soft lavender, where the light narrows into speech.

items.note: Notice any pressure in the throat and breathe around it, never through force.

units.title: Heart
units.intro: Add the heart: rose pink, the largest sphere, the seat of the circulation.

items.note: The heart centre carries the practice. Give it the most time.

units.title: Loins
units.intro: Add the loins: deep violet, where the light gathers before descending.

items.note: Gathering is not grasping. Let the violet hold without pulling.

units.title: Feet
units.intro: Add the feet: the quartered earth tones grounding the whole pillar.

items.note: A pillar with no foundation is a fantasy. Feel the feet.

units.title: The circulation
units.intro: The whole week in one sit: five centres, then the circulation down the front and up the spine with the breath.

items.note: If the circuit runs on its own, let it. If not, return to the heart.

title: Trika prep week
intro: Seven days of foundation for Abhinavagupta and VBT study: steady breath, the turn of the breath, and recognition. Ten minutes a day. Initiated practices are not here: when the gap is steady, take the next step with a qualified teacher in the tradition.
author: wiser

units.title: Settle
units.intro: The home base: ease through the body with the breath.

items.note: Where is the breath clearest today? That is your seat for the week.

units.title: The turn
units.intro: Notice where the in-breath becomes the out-breath. Rest there; hold nothing.

items.note: Did you find the turning, or the idea of it? Either is fine — noted, not judged.

units.title: Recognition
units.intro: One sutra slowly, then look: does anything appear outside awareness?

items.note: Write one sentence on what recognition felt like versus what you thought about it.

units.title: Return to ease
units.intro: Same foundation, deeper seat. The gap work needs a rested body.

items.note: Compare today with day 1: steadier, sleepier, brighter? Log it plainly.

units.title: Longer turn
units.intro: Same gap practice, full sit. Let attention fall in; never force it.

items.note: If strain appears, drop back to ease. The gap is found, not made.

units.title: Recognition again
units.intro: Same contemplation, fresh experience. Sound, thought, feeling — inside or outside?

items.note: One line for the journal: what was recognised, and by what?

units.title: The week in one sit
units.intro: Ease, then the turn, then recognition — one short sit chaining all three in order.

items.note: Which of the three is your door? That is what you take to a teacher next.

title: VBT Foundations
intro: Seven contemplative practices from the Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra, in a progression from the breath to daily life (not the text's own order): the turn of the breath, the gap between objects, inner sound, the body as awareness, the sense spaces, spaciousness, and the end-of-twelve through the day. Each is a quiet sit you can do on your own. The rest of the text (breath retention, mantra, the subtle-body practices) is learned from a qualified teacher: when one of these becomes your door, take it to a teacher in the tradition.
author: wiser

units.title: Breath-pause
units.intro: The first practice the text presents: resting in the gap between the in-breath and the out-breath.

items.note: Did you find the turning, or the idea of it? Either is fine — noted, not judged.

units.title: The gap between thoughts
units.intro: When the mind lets go of one thing and before it takes up the next, rest in the middle. Build on day 1's steadiness.

items.note: How long was the gap today? One thought-width, or longer?

units.title: Inner sound
units.intro: Listen to the subtle inner sound until sound dissolves into silence.

items.note: What quality was the sound — ring, hum, tone, silence? Log it plainly.

units.title: Body as consciousness
units.intro: Conceive of the body — or the whole universe — as nothing but consciousness. A felt sense, not an idea.

items.note: Did the body-sense shift, or was it the same body with a different label? Both are data.

units.title: Inner and outer spaces
units.intro: A sense contact — the outer space where it arrives, the inner space where it is received, both as one field.

items.note: Which side did attention collapse into — inner or outer? That is the habit to notice.

units.title: Spaciousness
units.intro: The space of the room, the space inside the body, the skin as a thin wall between: one open field.

items.note: When did the mind grasp for something solid? What did it grasp at?

units.title: The end-of-twelve through the day
units.intro: Not a sitting practice. A few times today, let attention touch the space just above the crown for a breath or two, then carry on.

items.note: How many times today did you remember? The remembering is the practice, not the count.
